facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
difficulty combing her hair and rising from a chair
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
without fever or weight loss
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
leukopenia (WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL)
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
elevated C-reactive protein (18.8 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (109.2 mm/hr)
bilateral sacroiliitis
bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement

support_spans: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
bilateral sacroiliitis

contradict_spans: normal creatine kinase (39 U/L)
electromyography and repeat creatine kinase were normal
concepts.why: The patient's progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and dysphagia, along with the laboratory findings of microcytic anemia and elevated inflammatory markers, support the diagnosis of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.

support_spans: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
contradict_spans: normal creatine kinase (39 U/L)

concepts.why: The patient's progressive proximal muscle weakness, symmetric muscle strength, and microcytic anemia, along with the history of thyroiditis, support the diagnosis of Thyroiditis-related myopathy.
It explains the uncovered finding of leukopenia, which is a common feature of systemic JIA.

rationales.F01: Progressive proximal muscle weakness is a hallmark of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
rationales.F04: Dysphagia is a common symptom in Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
rationales.F06: Symmetric muscle strength reduction is characteristic of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
rationales.F10: Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicate active inflammation, common in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
rationales.F11: Bilateral sacroiliitis is a feature of certain types of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
